subject: th-cont
title: TH.CONT.-----PROJ.DY-----AFL.
description: Second diagram on page 444 — a triple-crossing rather than a simple two-axis crossing. The triple-axis is the structural payload of MP(I)-18's argument that there is a *second* route through alternative functionalism beyond the Coltrane/King center-platform: TH-CONT (thrust continuance — the form's forward motion) is crossed with PROJ-DY (projectional dynamics) which is in turn crossed with AFL (affinity alignment — the receiving condition that makes the projection land). TH-CONT sits on the left with the subject-arrow, and the main line bends at PROJ-DY before rising to AFL. PRI-INFO (principle information) descends from the TH-CONT–PROJ-DY stretch; AF-DY (affinity dynamics) and ISTF branch from PRI-INFO, and AFTO branches from ISTF. PROJ-DY sits at the middle of the axis as the *bridging* center; ALT-C-PG (alternative composite progressionalism) rises from the PROJ-DY–AFL stretch, CN-INFO (controlled information) branches from ALT-C-PG to the top-right, and APP-RDEF (applied redefinitions) hangs from CN-INFO. AFL is the partner-axis on the right; SOC-RT (social reality) hangs from the PROJ-DY–AFL stretch. Structural argument: the three-axis structure is how this 'second route' actually works — thrust-continuance does not reach affinity-alignment directly. Projectional-dynamics is the necessary middle term. Single crossings cannot represent the route; only the triple-axis can.
